title: Latency safety-net: pin windows and throttle strategy for multi-region routing
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Problem: During spikes and partial regional outages we observe increased tail latency for hosted inference requests. Current steering uses coarse geo-preferences and simple hedging which leads to either excessive cross-region failovers (costly) or local latency degradation (customer-facing).

Goal: Define and prototype a latency safety-net routing policy that combines short-term 'pin windows' to preserve locality when healthy, capacity-aware throttles, and a circuit-breaker-driven failforward mechanism. The policy must respect SLOs (p95/p99), minimize cross-region egress and cold-starts, and allow graceful degradation to lighter/smaller model variants or cached prefixes when needed.
acceptance_criteria: Policy design doc reviewed and approved by Reliability and Serving Runtime teams
Prototype implemented in steerer service behind feature-flag for a single product route
Synthetic chaos test shows <2% increase in cross-region egress for targeted route compared to baseline, with p95 latency within SLO under 95th percentile load bursts
Circuit breaker transitions (open/half-open/closed) are recorded and alerting rules trigger on repeated open events
Deployment playbook for canary, rollback, and gradual ramp included in repo and Console rollout UI hooks wired
implementation_notes:
Design highlights: 1) Pin windows — when a request last routed successfully to a local region within T_pin (default 10s) we bias future requests for the same token/client to stay local unless local capacity signals degrade. 2) Capacity hints — each region publishes a short-lived capacity token count and queue-length-percentile to the central steer cache. 3) Soft throttle — per-region token-bucket that rejects or soft-fails based on remaining capacity credits; rejected requests are offered a fast-fail or reroute depending on client tier. 4) Circuit breaker — three levels: healthy, stressed (slow responses > p95_threshold), and tripped (error-rate or queue saturation). On tripped, traffic is directed to a failforward path (compatible model variant + routing to a reserve region). 5) Degraded compute modes — prefer cached prefix/KV responses or quantized model until local region recovers.

Trade-offs considered: stricter pinning reduces cross-region cost but can hurt latency during localized saturation. Long pin windows reduce jitter but reduce agility; chosen default is short (10s) with an exponential backoff policy. Token-bucket sizing is conservative initially and will be tuned against telemetry. Failforward to smaller models risks quality regressions; we add request-level tags for origin to support post-hoc quality evals.
rollout_plan:
1) Implement feature-flagged prototype on canary steerers for /v1/generate route (week 1-2). 2) Run synthetic traffic and soak tests with chaos (introduce delayed responses and partial region cpu pressure) (week 2). 3) Run controlled customer canary for internal power users (week 3). 4) Gradually widen to 10% of traffic, monitor SLOs and cost (week 4). 5) Full rollout after 2-week stabilization window and signoff.

Rollback criteria: sustained p99 exceedance > 3x baseline for 30 minutes, >0.5% increased 5xx rate, or repeated circuit-breaker flapping across multiple regions.
telemetry_queries: Dashboard: per-route p50/p95/p99 by region over time (Prometheus/Grafana)
notes_on_tests_and_results:
Initial unit tests validate token-bucket arithmetic and pin window TTL; integration in local cluster shows correct preference ordering. Chaos run 2026-03-05: simulated 30% CPU throttle in us-west-2 for 20 minutes; prototype diverted 12% of traffic cross-region and p95 rose 8% vs baseline but stayed within SLO for P0 customers. Observed circuit-breaker entered stressed mode twice; feedback: increase hysteresis on stressed -> tripped transition. Action: bump stressed threshold by 20% and add minimum open interval of 15s.

Quality note: failforward to smaller model produced measurable BLEU-like drop on eval prompts for summarization; we marked these requests with metadata to exclude from aggregated product quality stats and created a follow-up to test prompt-based graceful fallback (ENG-661508).
review_feedback:
- From Serving Runtime (Santiago Ruiz): ensure KV-cache awareness when deciding to failforward to quantized variant; cold-start penalty needs accounting.
- From PM (Marta Lopez): add customer-facing behavior document explaining possible short-lived quality regressions and opt-out for enterprise customers.
- From Security (Rohit Patel): ensure telemetry keys for pinning do not include raw user IDs; use hashed tokens.

All reviewers provisionally approved design subject to telemetry and canary results.
